title: ICE agents pepper spray pregnant US citizen in California, video shows
excerpt: Lizbeth Vargas Andrade, 23, was arrested after being pushed to the ground and on to her stomach, her attorney says
content_html:
US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents pepper-sprayed a pregnant US citizen and threw her to the ground during a protest in California on Sunday, according to her family’s attorney, who shared footage of the incident.

Lizbeth Vargas Andrade, 23, was filming and protesting the presence of several ICE officers outside the Stanislaus county jail in Modesto, in California’s central valley, before she was taken down by officers and arrested while she was lying on her stomach during a chaotic encounter.

Vargas Andrade, who is 12 weeks pregnant, said in a press conference on Sunday evening that she is part of a group of local residents who monitor ICE sightings, and that she had gone to the jail parking lot after agents were spotted in the area.

A commotion erupted when ICE agents moved to arrest a man who, it appeared, had just been released from the jail, video shows.

Footage filmed by Vargas Andrade’s husband, Adolfo Talavera, captured a tumultuous scene as several people protested the agents making the arrest. The circumstances of the man’s arrest were not immediately clear, and he has not been identified. Agents wore law enforcement vests and ICE badges, and at least two of them had masks covering their faces.

It was unclear what exactly happened right before Vargas Andrade’s arrest, with the sound on the footage repeatedly cutting out. One woman was heard screaming at the agents to get away from her and another cursed at the agents, telling them, “You should be embarrassed … you guys are so fucked up.”

Vargas Andrade had her phone in one hand as she and an agent then appeared to bump into each other, footage showed. That agent then grabbed her and started to handcuff her. Another agent then pulled out what appeared to be a pepper-spray canister and pointed it at the direction of Vargas Andrade and her husband who was filming.

The footage partially captured the agent deploying the pepper spray, though it was difficult to discern how long he sprayed it and where the chemicals landed. Soon after, the footage captured Talavera shouting, “She’s pregnant with child!” as the agents moved to detain his wife. Seconds later, two agents took Vargas Andrade to the ground where she was handcuffed on her stomach with her hands behind her back, before one of the agents moved her onto her side.

Vargas Andrade was taken into custody and transported to an ICE field office in Stockton, according to her attorney, Patrick Kolasinski. Vargas Andrade’s sister had called for an ambulance, which then arrived at the ICE facility and transported her to a hospital, her family and a local advocate said at the press conference.

Vargas Andrade said officers had told her she was accused of assaulting an ICE agent, an accusation she denied. She was released later that day, and she has not been charged with any crimes, according to Kolasinski.

Spokespeople for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) did not immediately respond to inquiries on Monday. A spokesperson for the Department of Justice (DoJ) declined to comment. A spokesperson for the Stanislaus sheriff’s office, which runs the jail, said sheriff deputies were not involved in Vargas Andrade’s arrest.

“They threw me to the ground, they maced me, then they handcuffed me,” Vargas Andrade recalled to reporters on Sunday night. “I told the ICE agent … ‘I’m pregnant, so don’t put your hands on me.’ … They right away threw me on the floor … I was burning. I couldn’t breathe. The mace went up my nose.”

Another ICE agent then gave her water to wash her face, she recalled.

“I got scared,” Talavera said. “I was like, what if she has a miscarriage?”

Vargas Andrade said she was particularly worried because she had suffered two previous pregnancy losses, but she said doctors did an ultrasound after the incident and did not identify any concerns.

The encounter happened amid reports of increased ICE activity in California’s central valley region, which is home to the state’s agricultural industry. DHS and the justice department have repeatedly accused anti-ICE protesters of assaulting agents, though many of those prosecutions in California have fallen apart in federal court.

“We’re not going to stop helping the community even though this happened,” Vargas Andrade said. “We want our immigrants to feel safe here.”
